verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "It will make a water landing around 8:07 p.m. ET in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California." (R1); "Splashing down in the Pacific Ocean on Friday near San Diego" (R2); "splashdown around 8:07 p.m. (5:07 p.m. PDT) Friday, April 10, off the coast of San Diego" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the splashdown location as Pacific Ocean off San Diego.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The Orion capsule is due to reenter Earth's atmosphere on Friday, April 10, 2026." (R1); "Floating in the Pacific Ocean on Friday" (R2); "Friday, April 10" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly confirm splashdown on Friday, April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "8:07 p.m.: Splashdown in the Pacific Ocean" (R1); "splashdown around 8:07 p.m. (5:07 p.m. PDT)" (R3); "splashdown at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Exact time matches across sources, including PDT conversion.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will re-enter Earth's atmosphere at 7:53 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "7:53 p.m.: Entry interface" (R1); "At 7:53 p.m., at an altitude of 400,000 feet, it hit ... entry interface" (R2); "Orion will reach ... entry interface ... at 7:53 p.m." (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Precise time for entry interface (re-entry) directly stated.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a 10-day mission around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "final day of their 10-day milestone mission to orbit the moon" (R1); "10 days in space" (R2); "approximate 10-day mission around the Moon" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as a 10-day mission around the Moon.

verifications.claim: Artemis II service module separation is scheduled at 7:33 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "7:33 p.m.: Crew module and service module separation" (R1); "At 7:33 p.m. the Orion crew capsule ... detached from the cylindrical service module" (R2); "service module will separate around 7:33 p.m." (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and date for service module separation confirmed.

verifications.claim: Artemis II re-entry into Earth's atmosphere is scheduled at 7:53 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "7:53 p.m.: Entry interface" on April 10 (R1); "At 7:53 p.m.... entry interface" on April 10 (R2); "at 7:53 p.m. as plasma forms... at 7:53 p.m." (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Precise time and date for atmospheric re-entry (entry interface) match.

verifications.claim: Artemis II splashdown in the Pacific Ocean is scheduled at 8:07 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "8:07 p.m.: Splashdown in the Pacific Ocean" on April 10 (R1); "splashdown at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time" April 10 Pacific (R2); "8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)" April 10 (R5)

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission brings back astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch of NASA and Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency" returned (R2); "NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Crew names exactly match and confirmed returned safely.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II astronauts orbited the Moon.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "mission to orbit the moon" but context is flyby/test; "journey around the moon"; "lunar flyby"; "around the Moon and back"; no orbital insertion mentioned, free-return trajectory (R2, R5)
verifications.reasoning: Mission was a flyby/loop around Moon on free-return trajectory, not entering lunar orbit.
